questions.def: Extraposition uses 'it' as a dummy subject to postpone the real subject.
questions.question: ___ crucial to submit the report on time.

questions.def: Extraposition is used to shift focus; 'it' introduces a clause.
questions.question: ___ believed that the suspect had fled the country.

questions.def: Extraposition requires 'it' + verb in the correct tense.
questions.question: ___ that the witness is unreliable.

questions.def: 'It was' is used to introduce news or reported information.
questions.question: ___ reported that the company profits increased.

questions.def: 'It is' introduces a clause describing something essential.
questions.question: ___ essential for him to attend the meeting.

questions.def: Passive voice 'It is believed' is common in extraposition.
questions.question: ___ that she will win the election.

questions.def: 'It' is the dummy subject in extraposition; 'that' follows.
questions.question: ___ surprised me that he resigned so suddenly.

questions.def: 'It's been' introduces a statement about a past experience.
questions.question: ___ a pleasure working with you on this project.

questions.def: Passive 'It is understood' conveys common knowledge or agreement.
questions.question: ___ that the deadline is next week.

questions.def: 'It is' introduces the expectation about future events.
questions.question: ___ expected that prices will rise soon.

questions.def: 'It's' is short for 'it is' and introduces a general truth.
questions.question: ___ difficult to learn a new language quickly.

questions.def: 'It was proven' indicates evidence confirming past events.
questions.question: ___ that he was at the scene of the crime.

questions.def: 'It seems' is a common introductory phrase in extraposition.
questions.question: ___ seems that the project will be delayed.

questions.def: 'It's' (it is) shows importance in a general statement.
questions.question: ___ important to consider all the options.

questions.def: 'It was noticed' signifies an observation or awareness.
questions.question: ___ that she wasn't at the meeting.

questions.def: 'It is' indicates uncertainty or lack of clarity.
questions.question: ___ unclear whether they will accept the offer.

questions.def: 'It is' stresses the urgency or importance of action.
questions.question: ___ vital that we address this issue immediately.

questions.def: 'It was reported' introduces factual information or news.
questions.question: ___ that several people were injured.

questions.def: 'It's surprising' expresses astonishment at a situation.
questions.question: ___ surprising how quickly he adapted.

questions.def: 'It's' emphasizes the importance of an action for someone.
questions.question: ___ important for you to get some rest.

questions.def: 'It is expected' expresses anticipated future events.
questions.question: ___ that the economy will improve.

questions.def: 'It's a shame' expresses disappointment about a past event.
questions.question: ___ a shame that they cancelled the event.

questions.def: 'It is' suggests prudent action in a particular situation.
questions.question: ___ advisable to consult a lawyer in this case.

questions.def: Extraposition requires 'it' as a placeholder when the subject is a clause.
questions.question: ___ believed that the Earth was flat for centuries.

questions.def: Extraposition with 'it' + 'be' is used with adjectives like 'crucial'.
questions.question: ___ crucial to submit the report on time.

questions.def: 'It is' should replace 'Is' to use extraposition correctly.
questions.question: Is important to regularly back up your data.

questions.def: 'It seems' introduces a clause using extraposition, acting as a placeholder.
questions.question: ___ that he has changed his mind.

questions.def: Extraposition using 'it' as a subject before 'to work' is correct.
questions.question: ___ a pleasure to work with such a dedicated team.

questions.def: 'It is' used with adjectives like 'essential' needs 'it' for extraposition.
questions.question: ___ essential that all staff attend the meeting.

questions.def: 'It is considered' is needed for extraposition, not just 'Considered'.
questions.question: Considered that the new policy is unfair.
